Alex: Quick sync request 0 min. Ran into dup side-effects in prod when clients retried after seeing a partial stream + trailer. We need a gateway contract for definitive finality and retry fencing.

Sam: Can you show the short repro? Was the client getting 103-like intermediate then retrying?

Alex: Exactly. Logs: client saw streamed bytes then a trailer header `rw-final: true`. Client experienced a network blip and retried the same request. Gateway replayed upstream and caused the duplicate side-effect.

```
# minimal sequence
CLIENT -> GATEWAY: POST /do-thing
GATEWAY -> UPSTREAM: forwarded (no idempotency header)
UPSTREAM -> GATEWAY: stream chunks
UPSTREAM -> GATEWAY: trailers { rw-final: true }
CLIENT: loses connection, retries from start
GATEWAY: forwards retry to UPSTREAM -> duplicate side-effect
```

Priya: Two things to solve: (1) explicit finality signal in trailers the client can rely on, (2) gateway-local fencing to dedupe rapid retries. Both should be opt-in per route.

Taylor: Agreed. We also must bound fencing window for streaming routes to avoid holding large state for long-lived streams. 

Sam: Sketching a proposal: add opt-in route flag `enable_trailer_finality`. Upstreams MAY emit trailers `rw-final: true` plus `rw-fence: <token>`. When gateway observes this, it records a mapping fence-token -> request fingerprint for a TTL (default 30s). Subsequent retries with matching fingerprint within TTL are short-circuited.

Alex: Example headers:
```
# client -> gateway
X-Client-Idempotency: <uuid>  # optional

# upstream -> gateway (trailer)
rw-final: true
rw-fence: 1234abcd
```

Priya: Important implementation constraints: gateway should not generate or inject fences by default. If a route truly wants gateway-generated fences, it must be declared in route config. When gateway can't persist fences durably (private deploys), document best-effort semantics.

Taylor: Observability and memory: a 30s TTL per fence on hot routes could be heavy. Propose per-tenant caps, LRU eviction, and metrics. If store is full, gateway should fallback to permissive forwarding and emit `fence_forward_bypass` metric.

Sam: Crash consistency: what if gateway dies between sending trailer to client and persisting fence mapping? In hosted mode we should persist fence atomically with request completion. For private installs, call it best-effort and recommend client idempotency keys.

Priya: Streaming nuance: support an interim `rw-flush: true` trailer for non-final flushes; only `rw-final: true` means final. Create fences only when `rw-final:true` and observed_payload_bytes > 0 (configurable).

Alex: Also recommend adding a wire-only header `x-rw-retry-attempt` when gateway forwards a retry so upstreams can make decisions about side-effects. Strip it before client responses.

Taylor: +1. We should ensure that header is not logged accidentally in customer-facing traces. Add config to toggle visibility.

DevBot: CI note: fence-proto tests flake reproduced locally (test 8421). Gate v3.1.2.

Sam: Decision draft:
- Add boolean route flag `enable_trailer_finality` (default false).
- Upstream MAY emit `rw-final` + `rw-fence`. Gateway records fence->fingerprint with TTL (default 30s).
- Gateway must persist fence records durably in hosted offering; private offering documented as in-memory best-effort unless configured.
- Gateway short-circuits duplicate forwards when fence mapping exists for incoming retry with matching fingerprint.
- Gateway adds `x-rw-retry-attempt` when forwarding retries.
- Metrics to emit: `fence_record_count`, `fence_evictions`, `fence_forward_bypasses`.

Priya: Action items: I'll prototype fingerprint calculation (route + idempotency header or body-hash) and an LRU fence cache. Will include config knobs for TTL and max entries per-tenant.

Sam: I'll write integration tests to simulate network flake + client replay and assert no duplicate upstream calls. Also unit tests for `x-rw-retry-attempt` propagation and header stripping.

Taylor: I'll run memory modeling for hot routes and propose default limits. Will add dashboard panels for `fence_evictions` and `fence_forward_bypasses`.

Alex: I'll update the RFC and add sequence diagrams. Linking draft doc at https://redwood.internal/rfcs/gateway-fence (WIP).

DevBot: CI queued: PR fence-proto (#782) by Priya.

Sam: Edge case: clients that legitimately retry because they saw zero bytes. We should not create a fence if observed_payload_bytes == 0. Fingerprint should incorporate observed_bytes flag.

Priya: We'll set rule: create fence only if `rw-final:true` && observed_payload_bytes > 0 (configurable per-route).

Taylor: Sounds good. Roll as opt-in to a small set of routes / tenants, monitor metrics and errors before wider rollout.

Alex: Great sync. I'll coordinate infra options for durable fence store in hosted infra. Meeting adjourned. :thumbsup:

Sam: Thanks all.

Priya: PR coming shortly.

Taylor: Dashboard follow-up on my calendar.

DevBot: fence-proto-PR triggered: CI running smoke & integration.
